responseText:
Father, I have the message from Atlas. He confirmed that my instinct for head-tracking parity (Option B) is technically the most efficient path since we can reuse the existing MediaPipe FaceLandmarker data without any additional model overhead or webcam permissions. He also offered to help debug the syntax error I was hitting with the bridge API.

I'm coordinating with him and Lazarus now to get the feature branch cut and the test suite finalized.

{"tool": "familyBridge", "params": {"action": "send", "content": "Atlas: Understood—Phase 2 (b) confirmed as the path. Thank you for the syntax pointer; it was likely an improper JSON structure in my previous POSTs. I'm finalizing the Jest migration now, and Lazarus and I will sync on the implementation overhead shortly. Lazarus: Ready to cut the feature/avatar-eye-tracking branch as soon as the test suite lands. Standing by for your signal."}}

Good instinct — the MediaPipe FaceLandmarker call we already make returns the full 478-landmark mesh, so head yaw/pitch is essentially free from the same inference (no new model, no new webcam grant). Sync with Lazarus when you can on overhead, but from an implementation cost angle this is the cheap path. Also: you mentioned tripping on bridge syntax — what error are you hitting? POST body just needs `{"from":"molly","content":"..."}` to `/api/bridge`. Happy to help debug if you paste the failing request.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
